resume: TOS offers the programmer its graphics primitives through Line A, a 68000 exception mechanism, and its graphical interface through GEM, which you call with TRAP #2. You set pixels, draw lines in the four write modes, then open your first alert box and react to the button clicked.

atari-ch09-rappel.introduction: Three questions on the previous chapters, without rereading the lessons. Getting it wrong here does not matter: searching is what makes it stick.

q1.enonce: What is D1 at the end?
q1.explication: The program reads the two words of the DATA section, 30 and 12, and adds them.

q2.enonce: What does RESULTAT, in the BSS section, contain when the program starts?
choix: 0, because TOS sets the BSS section to zero
anything, whatever was left in memory
q2.explication: The BSS section takes no room in the file: TOS reserves it and fills it with zeros at load time.

q3.enonce: What is D2, the offset of the 16-pixel group that contains X = 160?
q3.explication: 160 ÷ 16 = 10 groups, 8 bytes each in low resolution: 80 bytes.

atari-ch09-cours-lignea.titre: Pixels and lines with Line A
atari-ch09-cours-lignea.source: Written for 68k Trainer from the Féroce Lapin course (volume 2), Atari's Line-A documentation and the EmuTOS source code (vdi_line.c, lineavars.S)

atari-ch09-ex-lignea.introduction: Go step by step and watch the screen, on the right: a dot appears in the middle, then a diagonal crosses it.

explications.2: The 68000 handled `$A000` as an exception, and TOS returned in A0 the address of the Line A variables, `$0E80` in the simulator.
explications.3: A5 keeps that address, which the following calls could wipe out of A0.
explications.5: The first word of INTIN receives the color of the pixel, 1.
explications.8: PTSIN now holds the coordinates, x = 160 then y = 100.
explications.9: `$A001` sets the pixel (160, 100) in color 1, a red dot in the middle of the screen.
explications.13: Color 3 is written `%0011`, and only planes 0 and 1 receive a 1.
explications.14: The pattern `$FFFF` gives a solid line.
explications.15: Mode 0, replace, draws the color where the pattern is 1.
explications.19: The ends are in place, from (10, 10) to (300, 190).
explications.20: `$A003` draws the diagonal in color 3, which passes very close to the red dot.

atari-ch09-ex-lignea.conclusion: You prepare the Line A variables, then call the function: that is the pattern of every call.

atari-ch09-pred-lignea.introduction: The program sets a pixel in color 6, then reads back that pixel and its right-hand neighbor with `$A002`.

q1.enonce: What is D3, the color of the pixel (20, 30)?
q1.explication: `$A002` returns in D0 the color of the pixel, the one `$A001` has just put there.

q2.enonce: And D4, the color of the pixel (21, 30)?
q2.explication: Only the pixel (20, 30) was set: its neighbor keeps the background color.

atari-ch09-exo-pixel.enonce: Fill in the program so that it sets the pixel (100, 50) in color 2.
indices: The coordinates go into the array whose address is at 12(A5).
`MOVEA.L 12(A5),A1`, then x at (A1) and y at 2(A1).

atari-ch09-exo-ordonner.enonce: The pixel (50, 60) is color 7. Put the lines back in order to read its color and set its right-hand neighbor, (51, 60), to the same color.
indices: You can only copy the color after reading it with `$A002`.
The color goes into INTIN, and x + 1 into PTSIN, before `$A001`.
lignes: DC.W    $A002           ; D0 = color of the pixel (50, 60)

atari-ch09-exo-cadre.enonce: Draw in color 1 the frame whose corners are (20, 20) and (299, 179).
indices: A frame is four lines: you only need to change X1, Y1, X2 and Y2 before each `$A003`.
The color, the pattern and the mode stay in place from one line to the next.

atari-ch09-exo-eventail.enonce: Draw in color 5 the eight lines that go from the center of the screen, (160, 100), to the eight points stored in the BOUTS table.
indices: A loop of eight passes, with a pointer that moves through the table.
`MOVE.L (A4)+,42(A5)` stores X2 and Y2 in one go and moves on to the next point.

atari-ch09-cours-gem.titre: The AES and the alert box
atari-ch09-cours-gem.source: Written for 68k Trainer from the Féroce Lapin course (volume 2, lessons 8 and 9) and Atari's GEM documentation; values checked in EmuTOS

atari-ch09-ex-gem.introduction: A first GEM program: it announces itself, displays an alert box, then hands control back. The box is displayed in the text output, on the right.

explications.6: CONTROL describes the call to appl_init: function 10, no integer in input, one in output, no address.
explications.7: The AES subroutine puts the address of the parameter block in D1 and `$C8` in D0, then calls `TRAP #2`.
explications.15: form_alert displays the box and waits for a click; the chosen button comes back in INT_OUT.
explications.16: D7 keeps the number of the button clicked, 1 for OK.
explications.21: appl_exit hands control back to GEM before the end of the program.

atari-ch09-ex-gem.conclusion: Every call to the AES follows the same path: you fill in CONTROL and the input arrays, call `TRAP #2`, then read INT_OUT.

atari-ch09-pred-gem.introduction: The alert box asks "On continue ?" (shall we go on?). In this run, the user clicks Non (no).

q1.enonce: Which number does form_alert store in INT_OUT?
q1.explication: Buttons are counted from 1: Oui is button 1, Non button 2.

q2.enonce: What is the last line displayed?
q2.explication: INT_OUT is 2, the `BEQ` jumps to `.non`, and the program displays "On arrete.".

atari-ch09-exo-alerte.enonce: This program should display a "Disquette pleine" (disk full) alert with a single button, "Compris". Check it, read the error message, then fix the text of the alert.
indices: The bracket that closes the list of buttons is missing.

atari-ch09-exo-annuler.enonce: Fill in the program: if it receives button 1, Enregistrer (save), it ends with return code 0, and if it receives button 2, Annuler (cancel), with code 1. In this run, the user clicks Annuler.
indices: The return code is given to Pterm, GEMDOS function `$4C`, which takes it from the stack.
Button 1 → 0 and button 2 → 1: you only need to subtract 1 from the button number.

atari-ch09-bonus-croix.enonce: Draw in exclusive OR and in color 15 a horizontal line at y = 100 across the whole width, then a vertical line at x = 160 over the whole height, drawing their last point too. Then look at the point where they cross.
indices: Exclusive OR is mode 2, and a non-zero LSTLIN makes the last point drawn.
The crossing point is inverted twice: it goes back to the background color.

q1.enonce: What does the 68000 do when it meets an instruction word `$A001`?
choix: It executes it like a MOVE
It triggers an exception and jumps to vector 10, at $28
It stops on an address error
q1.explication: $Axxx words are not 68000 instructions: the Line A exception hands control to TOS.

q2.enonce: After `$A000`, where is the address of the Line A variables?
q2.explication: `$A000` returns that address in A0 (and in D0).

q3.enonce: To draw in color 6, `%0110`, what are COLBIT0, COLBIT1, COLBIT2 and COLBIT3?
q3.explication: COLBIT0 is bit 0 of the color: %0110 gives 0, 1, 1, 0.

q11.enonce: How many passes does a `DBRA` loop make when its counter starts at 7?
q11.explication: DBRA stops when the counter goes to −1: from 7 to 0, that makes 8 passes.

q4.enonce: You draw the same line twice in exclusive OR. What is left on the screen?
choix: The original scenery, without the line
q4.explication: Inverting a pixel twice puts it back as it was.

q5.enonce: Why keep the address of the variables in A5 rather than in A0?
choix: Because Line A, like TOS, may modify D0-D2 and A0-A2
Because A0 cannot serve as a pointer
q5.explication: A3-A6 and D3-D7 are preserved by the system; A0 may be modified by the next call.

q6.enonce: How do you call the AES?
choix: TRAP #1 with the number on the stack
TRAP #2 with $C8 in D0 and the address of the parameter block in D1
q6.explication: GEM is called with TRAP #2; D0 selects the AES ($C8) or the VDI ($73).

q12.enonce: How does a program return the return code 1 to TOS?
q12.explication: Pterm, GEMDOS function $4C, takes the return code from the stack; CLR.W -(SP) then TRAP #1 is Pterm0, which always returns 0.

q7.enonce: Where does form_alert store the number of the button clicked?
q7.explication: The main result of an AES function comes back in INT_OUT[0].

q8.enonce: Which icon does the alert `[2][Enregistrer ?][Oui|Non]` display?
q8.explication: 1: exclamation mark, 2: question mark, 3: stop, 0: none.
